newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: World Bank criticises planned Slovak budget gap.
newsitem.headline: World Bank criticises planned Slovak budget gap.

text.p: The World Bank has criticised Slovakia's plan to run a budget deficit in 1997 instead of continuing a balanced fiscal policy, the daily Pravda reported on Friday.

The paper quoted a World Bank report as saying that after 1996's planned balanced budget for the public sector next year's fiscal deficit is expected to total slightly under 20 billion crowns, or three percent of the planned GDP.
"The World Bank considers this as a radical worsening of the development (of the budget)," the report said.
The Slovak parliament passed the 1997 budget last Friday. The World Bank warned that a large fiscal deficit can cause problems in the monetary sphere.
The bank also called for Slovakia to curb the current account deficit from this year's eight percent of GDP to three percent.
